question_record.context: During an investigation of a security incident involving an ongoing hands-on-keyboard attack via the Impacket toolkit, it was found that a suspicious command was executed. This tool is noted for its use in lateral movement across the network and in deploying ransomware or other payloads. A relevant piece in the investigation is the `lsass.exe` process, with a Process ID of 780, which might indicate an attacker's activity on the system.
question_record.question: Can you identify the account name of the system executable that was renamed and launched?
solution: Suspicious execution of a command via Impacket toolkit was observed with the command line `powershell.exe -encodedcommand qwa6afwauwbjahiaaqbwahqacwbcafiazqbuageabqblafaabwb3aguacgbzaggazqbsagwalgbwahmamqa=` at `2024-07-02t09:48:12.7628138z`, with Process ID `6808`.
A Windows executable file that has been renamed was launched using the `SYSTEM` account.

16.name: Ongoing hands-on-keyboard attack via Impacket toolkit
16.description:
Suspicious execution of a command via Impacket was observed on this device. This tool connects to other hosts to explore network shares and execute commands. Attackers might be attempting to move laterally across the network using this tool. This usage of Impacket has often been observed in hands-on-keyboard attacks, where ransomware and other payloads are installed on target devices.

Corresponding TA for this IOA: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/ff7e4fff-dde3-49be-9a06-7f63a490996d/analystreport

27.name: System executable renamed and launched
27.description: A Windows executable file that has been renamed was launched. Attackers might be attempting to use the executable to perform malicious activities, such as running malicious code or connecting to an attacker-controlled network address. By changing the path or file name of a system executable, attackers can avoid certain behavior-based detection technologies that rely on default paths and file names.

FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
